livability.title: About Livability Index
livability.intro: The Livability Index shows how well each home meets your conditions. Turn a condition on and set what is OK for you: a home that meets it scores 100 on it, and less the further it falls short. The index is the average over the conditions that are on, then reduced by the climate risks you care about. Colours use a fixed 0–100 scale in four bands (Great, Good, Partial, Poor match); Boost contrast fits them to the visible area instead.
livability.walk: Walking minutes from the building's entrance to the nearest supermarket, pharmacy, park, school, kindergarten, clinic, metro, café, restaurant and beach, along the street network (OSM); parks and beaches count to their edge. A service within your limit counts fully, fading to 0 at {{factor}}× the limit; one beyond 1.5 km counts 0. The score is the share of your services within reach — you can pick which ones count.
livability.noise: Lden (day-evening-night level, dB) along every exposed facade of the building — street and courtyard sides — averaged by facade length: the noise of a typical window, modelled 4 m above the ground. Within your limit → 100; {{falloff}} dB over it → 0. For reference: 45 dB a quiet courtyard, 55 a calm street, 65 a busy street, 75 a main road; the WHO recommends below 53 dB. Barcelona: the city's 2022 strategic noise map; 14 AMB municipalities: their 2022 official maps (SICA), a different model that reads a few dB louder.
livability.core: Walking minutes to each place you pick (Sagrada Família, Plaça Catalunya…), along the street network from the building. A place within your limit counts fully, fading to 0 at {{factor}}× the limit; the score is the share of your places within reach.
livability.price: Official average sale price €/m² of the building's barri (Barcelona) or municipality (Generalitat de Catalunya, INCASOL) — the area's average, not the price of a specific flat. At or below your budget → 100; {{pct}}% over it → 0.
livability.locals: How satisfied residents are with living in their barri (0–10), from Barcelona's municipal services survey (ESM, 2022–2026, about 30,000 interviews). Barris with few interviews are pulled towards their wider area (gran barri). At or above your minimum → 100; {{falloff}} point below it → 0. Barcelona city only — buildings outside count as missing data. Barris with few interviews also count as missing data.
livability.age: Off by default. Tick the eras of construction you like: a building of a liked era scores 100, any other 0, fading over a few years at the edges of an era. Year of construction from Catastro; a renovation is shown in the building card but does not change the score. Catastro gives 1900 for many old buildings whose exact year is unknown, so 1900 counts for both neighbouring eras.
livability.risk: Climate risks are not averaged in — they reduce the score of exposed buildings only: score × (1 − strength/10 × risk). Safe buildings keep their score; strength 10 on a building in the highest-risk zone drives it to 0.
livability.river: River flood risk — the building touches one of the official river flood zones (ACA): 10-year zone counts fully, 100-year 60%, 500-year 25%. Rivers overflowing only — rain water on streets is the separate Street flooding risk.
livability.fire: Wildfire risk — the building touches the wildland–urban interface (Protecció Civil, zones around forests ≥ 5 ha) × the hazard of the nearest forest (Generalitat structural wildfire hazard map 2024, classes 1–10), fading with distance. A static hazard map, not a forecast; recent burned areas are not reflected.
livability.street: Street flooding risk — how deep the water gets at the building's door in a 10-year and a 100-year rain (RESCCUE drainage model, Barcelona only). Depth is weighted smoothly: water up to 10 cm stays in the gutter and counts 0, 50 cm or more counts fully. Matters most for ground-floor flats, basements and underground parking.

noise.what: Barcelona Strategic Noise Map 2022 — total combined exposure: road traffic, railways, industry, and leisure/entertainment venues. All sources that contribute to residential noise are included.
noise.lden: Lden (Level day-evening-night) is a 24-hour weighted average in dB(A) that penalises evening and night noise — when people are more sensitive to disturbance:
noise.dataLink: Barcelona Strategic Noise Map · Open Data BCN
noise.title: Noise · Lden dB(A)

flood.what: Areas the Catalan Water Agency (ACA) expects to be flooded when a river or stream overflows, for three return periods. A 10-year flood has a 10% chance of happening in any given year (≈ 96% over 30 years); a 100-year flood 1% (≈ 26% over 30 years); a 500-year flood 0.2% (≈ 6% over 30 years). The 500-year zone is the official floodable zone in Spanish planning law.
flood.not: This layer shows river overflow only, without water depth. For flooding of streets during heavy rain (with depth) see Street flooding (heavy rain). Coastal flooding is not included.
flood.dataLink: ACA — Agència Catalana de l'Aigua, flood zones (WFS)
flood.title: River flood zones · ACA — by probability

street.what: Modelled water depth on streets when a heavy downpour overwhelms the sewer network — a 10-year rain (10% chance in any year) or a 100-year rain (1%). From the RESCCUE 1D/2D model of Barcelona's drainage, current climate. Water below 10 cm stays in the gutter and is not shown.
street.who: Matters most for ground-floor flats, basements and underground parking — water gets in over door steps and down ramps. For flats higher up it mostly means the street is impassable for a while.
street.notTitle: Not the same as river flood zones
street.not: River flood zones (blue) show where a river overflows, by probability, without depth. This layer shows rain water on streets, by depth. Barcelona only; the model dates from ~2020 and does not include storm tanks built since.
street.data: Data: RESCCUE project (BCASA / Aquatec) · Atles de resiliència, Ajuntament de Barcelona. No explicit open-data license.
street.title: Street flooding · water depth (RESCCUE)

wildfire.forest: Generalitat de Catalunya structural wildfire hazard map 2024: how easily each 100 m forest cell would burn and how intense a fire would be, from 1 (lowest) to 10 (highest) relative to all of Catalonia. Only forest and natural land is rated — built-up areas are transparent. It is a static map, not a daily forecast; burned areas after 2024 are not reflected.
wildfire.wui: Protecció Civil zones around forests of 5 ha or more where a wildfire can reach buildings. Housing developments here have legal fire-prevention duties under Llei 5/2003 (perimeter firebreaks, hydrants, plot clearing).
wildfire.title: Wildfire hazard 2024
